item.title: Germany's Uniper signs 15-year gas import deal with Norway's Equinor
item.description: Germany's Uniper has signed a deal to import more than 30 terawatt hours of gas a year from Equinor from 2027, the companies said on Monday, reinforcing Norway's position as the key supplier to Europe's biggest economy.
item.dc:creator: Nora Buli, Christoph Steitz
item.content:encoded: Germany's Uniper (UN0k.DE) has signed a deal to import more than 30 terawatt hours of gas a year from Equinor (EQNR.OL) from 2027, the companies said on Monday, reinforcing Norway's position as the key supplier to Europe's biggest economy. The deal, equivalent to around 2.8 billion cubic metres of natural gas per year, runs until the end of 2041, and equates to nearly 3% of Germany's annual gas imports. Norway supplied 44% of Germany's gas imports, according to network regulator Bundesnetzagentur, taking Russia's place as the largest supplier after Moscow ended most energy ties with Europe following its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The contract with Equinor marks Uniper's latest effort to diversify its supplies and follows its [USN:L6N43U0J6 TEXT:"agreement"] with Canada as companies seek to bolster energy security after shortages linked to the Iran war. "For us it's really important that we rebuild our portfolio," Uniper CEO Michael Lewis told Reuters after signing the deal in Stavanger, Norway, adding the agreement could not come at a more important moment. "When you look at the turbulence in the energy markets over the last few years, it's critical that we diversify our energy supplies. Different suppliers, different routes, whether that's pipeline or LNG," Lewis said. LONG-TERM GAS DEMAND Both Lewis and Equinor CEO Anders Opedal stressed the importance of Norwegian supply for European energy security. The agreement also sends a strong signal from European industry that Norwegian gas will remain in demand for years to come, Opedal told Reuters. "This is the first contract that goes into the 2040s," he said. The companies also said they would expand cooperation on lower-emission gas projects, highlighting the relatively low carbon intensity of Norwegian gas, although they did not provide further details. Lewis said gas would remain a necessary transition fuel as Germany seeks to phase out coal, arguing that increased gas use in the near term could lower emissions while supporting longer-term decarbonisation goals in combination with carbon capture technology. Sources previously [USN:L1N42A0NN TEXT:"told"] Reuters that Equinor is among the parties interested in state-owned Uniper, which Berlin is seeking to divest after rescuing the utility during Europe's energy crisis in 2022. Opedal declined to comment when asked whether Equinor had expressed interest in the stake.

item.description: Shah’s rejection of the two-stanza version also lies the suggestion that they are bigger nationalists and patriots than Gandhi, Tagore, Bose, Patel and Nehru.
item.dc:creator: D.K. Singh
item.content:encoded:
-->

3 things that are wrong with BJP’s Vande Mataram politics

In Modi-Shah’s rejection of the two-stanza version also lies the suggestion that they are bigger nationalists and patriots than Gandhi, Tagore, Bose, Patel and Nehru.

D.K. Singh

24 August, 2026 11:46 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

File photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah | Photo: T. Narayan | Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

T he BJP has put the Congress on the spot over nationalism again. Or so goes the chatter in political circles. See how the principal opposition party has dug itself into a hole over Vande Mataram, our national song.

Kerala Chief Minister VD Satheesan did away with the national song at the official flag-hoisting ceremony on Independence Day. His counterparts—DK Shiv a kumar, Revanth Reddy and Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu—in three other Congress-ruled states chose to comply with Amit Shah-led Home Ministry’s order to sing all six stanzas of Vande Mataram.

At the Congress headquarters in New Delhi, as the singing went beyond the second stanza, there were red faces all around. Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge were visibly dismayed. And, no, Sonia wasn’t asking for a chair for Kharge. Everybody saw what was happening. The Congress was at sixes and sevens about the six-stanza national song. The Gandhis should sack the general secretary (organisation), KC Venugopal, for making a joke of the party on such a sensitive issue.

Show Full Article

The BJP loved it. When it comes to issues related to nationalism or religion, trust the Congress to dig a hole for itself. And here was a blend of both. When the Congress Working Committee (CWC) later decided to stick to the original two-stanza Vande Mataram, the BJP doubled down. It accused the Opposition party of minority appeasement because there are references to Hindu goddesses—Durga, Kamala (Lakshmi) and Vanee (Saraswati)—in the fifth stanza.

On Saturday, when newly appointed office-bearers met at the BJP headquarters, cameras were in place for the six-stanza national song. Most of the leaders were just lip-syncing. Questioning others’ nationalism is easier; memorising six stanzas requires true belief and commitment. I would also lip-sync if I were asked to sing all six stanzas without a teleprompter or a written text.

Having said that, the government and the BJP expending all their time and energy on Vande Mataram shows they have learnt the wrong lessons from the drubbing they got from ‘cockroaches’: that they need to double down on performative nationalism and communal binary in their politics. This approach is problematic on at least three counts.

A disconnect with India First, it suggests their refusal to see the headwinds. As I was writing it on Sunday , I glanced at the headlines in the last two days’ newspapers strewn on the table. “Rashtrapati Bhawan announces, retracts Rahman visit statement,” read one headline. Basically, the President’s office virtually declared Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to India, only to withdraw it an hour later.

As we were discussing this flip-flop the previous evening in our newsroom, a colleague quipped, “basically, the left arm didn’t know what the right arm was doing”. This used to happen during the Manmohan Singh government, especially in its second term. When did this start happening in the Modi government? The Rashtrapati Bha v an blooper only drew attention to the fact that Dhaka was keeping New Delhi on tenterhooks. We invite their PM, and this is how they respond! Our Vishwaguru edifice can’t be crumbling like this!

I reached out for a Hindi paper. It had a screaming headline on the front page: “Skyrocketing sugar price before festivals: selling at Rs. 70 per kg, an increase of Rs.17 in one month.” I reached out to another Hindi paper to find another screaming headline: “Rahul sat on dharna at the police station for seven hours, only then FIR of youth injured with 200 pellets registered.”

So, a common man needs the opposition leader’s help to lodge an FIR even in the national capital. Think of the message it sent. Front pages could be a bit loud, I thought. I decided to flip through inside pages. On top of the business page was another headline: “Inflation reaches from travel to kitchen: rice, biscuit, car, tyre, paint costlier by 18 per cent.” Another front page headline was: “Reality of recruitments in the Central government: vacancies in the last one decade go from 4.2 lakhs to 8.24 lakhs.”

Where does the Vande Mataram headline fit on these pages? There appears to be a disconnect between what’s happening in ordinary people’s lives and how those in power view them. Do those running the government and the BJP really believe that four extra stanzas can answer all the questions people may have about 12 years of governance?

It would be delulu politics in Gen Z parlance. If those running the show know this, why are they so stuck on the national song issue, instead of trying to focus their energy on governance and address issues that are bringing the people to the streets for protest? There can be only two reasons—confidence or helplessness. Confident because they know how to win elections, and that’s the only thing that matters. Jo jita wahi Sikandar . Or helpless because they don’t know any other way.

The second problem with the BJP’s Vande Mataram politics is an implied suggestion that PM Modi and HM Shah are better than Mahatma Gandhi, Subhas Chandra Bose, Rabindranath Tagore, Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Patel put together. The freedom fighters, Nobel laureates, and composer of our national anthem had held extensive deliberations before they decided to go with only two stanzas of Vande Mataram as India’s national song. It was Sardar Patel who seconded the resolution on the two-stanza song at the 1937 CWC meeting.

In Modi-Shah’s rejection of the two-stanza version also lies the suggestion that they are bigger nationalists and patriots than Gandhi, Tagore, Bose, Patel and Nehru. It’s a flattering thought, for sure. Look at the level of confidence. The Constituent Assembly had adopted the two-stanza Vande Mataram as our national song. It has been changed to six stanzas simply by a Home Ministry order signed by a joint secretary. It amounts to belittling our Constitution-makers.

Also read: Indian politicians need to learn to take a joke

The Viksit Bharat question The third problem with the BJP’s Vande Mataram politics is that it seems to be driven by immediate political objectives, not long-term interests of the country. Modi sang the same two-stanza song on every Independence Day for 24 years—first as Gujarat CM and then the Prime Minister—happily. What suddenly happened in the 26th year?

The bigger question is whether a government that promises to make India a developed country by 2047 can afford to embark on a polarising mission. Let me cite just one instance. The Home Ministry’s February order also said, “In all schools, the day’s work may begin with community singing of the National Song. School authorities should make adequate provision in their programmes for popularising the singing of the National Song….”

On the face of it, it sounds like an innocuous suggestion. Think of a zealous BJP CM making the singing of a six-stanza national song mandatory in “all schools”—government, private, mad ra sas, missionary schools, et al. It can potentially create trouble in every village, kasba and town.

There goes the dream of a Viksit Bharat.

DK Singh is Political Editor at ThePrint. He tweets @dksingh73. Views are personal.

(Edited by Saptak Datta)

item.title: ノルウェー、ＥＵの立場にかかわらず北極圏資源開発継続＝エネ相
item.description:
Nora Buli Nerijus Adomaitis
[オスロ ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Nora Buli　Nerijus Adomaitis

[オスロ ２４日 ロイター] - ノルウェーのオースラン・エネルギー相はロイターに対し、欧州連合（ＥＵ）が北極圏における炭化水素供給のモラトリアム（一時停止措置）を支持しているものの、バレンツ海の石油・ガス資源開発を継続すると述べた。

「現在の地政学的・安全保障上の環境、そして資源事情を踏まえると、バレンツ海での活動を継続することは、ノルウェーと欧州双方の利益に資するものと確信している」と指摘。ノルウェーの主張がブリュッセルで受け止められていると考えているが、たとえＥＵがモラトリアムを支持し続けたとしても、バレンツ海の資源を開発するのはノルウェーの主権的権利だと付け加えた。

ＥＵは現在、環境上の理由から北極圏での新規掘削禁止を支持しているが、エネルギー安全保障への懸念を受けて、政策の見直しを検討している。

オースラン氏によると、ノルウェーは少なくとも２０３５年までは石油の生産と輸出をおおむね現在の水準に維持することを目指しており、その鍵を握るのがバレンツ海での生産だという。

item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ローソンは24日、コメ価格が下落していることを受けて、おにぎりを値下げすると明らかにした。手巻きおにぎりが対象で、値段を一律で10円引き下げる。

同社の広報担当者によると、価格改定は9月29日から。手巻きおにぎりの「 熟成紀州南高梅」は税込み194円から184円に、「シーチキンマヨネーズ」は同181円から171円にそれぞれ値下げする。

農林水産省によると、8月10日からの1週間にスーパーで販売されたコメ5キロ当たりの全国平均価格は、税込みで3191円だった。4000円を超えて推移していた販売価格は、26年1月以降、下落基調に転じた。

原材料の高騰や円安などによるコスト上昇を受けて、値上げする企業が相次ぐ中、あえて値下げに動く企業も一部で見られる。くら寿司は最低価格115円で提供していたすしメニューの一部について、110円に値下げすると20日に発表していた。

ローソンの広報担当者は、求めやすい価格で商品を提供することで、「結果として米の消費拡大につなげて行きたい」とも語った。

item.title: Shein fashions bizarre upside-down IPO
item.description: The online retailer is targeting a $27 bln valuation at best, almost 75% below its peak. Side deals mean it’ll pay some $3.5 bln, twice the IPO proceeds, to any invested at those higher levels. Professional risk-takers ought to wear their mistakes, not be compensated for them.
item.dc:creator: Katrina Hamlin
item.content:encoded: Shein’s IPO turns the concept of capital raising upside-down. The online retailer is now hoping to raise $1.8 billion in its looming stock market debut. But at the same time it will be paying around double that to investors in its private funding rounds since 2022 to make up for its shrunken valuation. In essence, that means these professional risk-takers are being compensated for their own mistakes. That's not how public listings are supposed to work. The problem stems from the near-75% decline in the value of Shein's equity, which stood at $98 billion in early 2022. Investors in a later round, where the company's worth had fallen to $64 billion, negotiated payouts in case it plummeted further. This March, the company extended the privilege to all who had sewn money into Shein at $60 billion or higher. That means the company now has to [USN:L4N44L004 TEXT:"stump up"] $3.5 billion in cash and another $120 million in stock to these irrationally exuberant venture capitalists. Sure, Shein has long insisted during its several attempts over the years to go public that it's not doing so because it needs the money. But it's bizarre indeed, to say the least, to push ahead with an IPO that costs the company twice what it's raising. Adding to the topsy-turvy nature of Shein's capital-raising saga, some of its current shareholders are coming back for more: Boyu Capital, General Atlantic and Tiger Global are among those to sign up as cornerstone investors for the offering, which will be Hong Kong’s largest this year. Given that Shein may yet deserve a deeper discount, they may be in for more pain. That's because even a $27 billion valuation looks punchy. Assume revenue hits $36 billion this year, based on annualising the adjusted first-quarter sales number. Assume 4.5% growth in 2027 and a net margin of around 3.5%, and Shein's net profit could hit $1.4 billion. Pop that on 20 times multiple, a tad below the 24.5 times Zara-owner Inditex (ITX.MC) sports, per Visible Alpha, and the equity would be worth what Shein wants IPO investors to pay for it. But the company is grappling with the end of import duty exemptions for low-value parcels in the U.S., new fees on such shipments in Europe, and investigations in both regions – which are its two largest markets. Sales grew only 1% in the first quarter, with a 2.5% net margin, after adjusting for one-off charges. And the 20 times multiple is overly generous: Inditex and other listed fashion peers have margins closer to 10%, as well as stronger sales growth. Sure, Shein could don a nattier performance than that, but it would take time to prove that any rapid recovery were sustainable. Its messy IPO is setting the scene for a financial fashion faux pas. Follow Katrina Hamlin on Bluesky and Linkedin . Online fashion retailer Shein Global will price its shares at up to HK$49.50 each according to a filing on August 24. At the upper end of the range, the company could raise HK$13.9 billion ($1.8 billion), implying a valuation of $26.8 billion. Shein will pay out as much as $2.2 billion in compensation to early investors, assuming the final offer price is at the low end of the range, and issue an additional 19.6 billion in stock, worth about $120 million. It is also paying out $1.3 billion in cash to holders of Series pre-D, D and D plus preferred shares, who bought in when the company was valued at $60 billion or more. Cornerstone investors led by existing shareholders Boyu, Tiger Global and General Atlantic have subscribed for about $383 million worth of Shein shares, the prospectus showed. Tencent, Greenwoods, Taikang Life and UBS Asset Management will also take stock. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: EEUU anuncia un "Día D económico" mientras Irán amenaza con detener todas sus exportaciones de crudo
item.description: Estados Unidos amenazó a Irán con lo que calificó como "la mayor ofensiva financiera jamás organizada", mientras se preparaba para poner en marcha el lunes unas sanciones económicas dirigidas contra los socios comerciales de Irán.
item.dc:creator: Yasmine Ghania, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: Estados Unidos amenazó a Irán con lo que calificó como "la mayor ofensiva financiera jamás organizada", mientras se preparaba para poner en marcha el lunes unas sanciones económicas dirigidas contra los socios comerciales de Irán. Irán, por su parte, prometió detener todas las exportaciones de petróleo del golfo Pérsico "si la guerra económica continúa". El secretario del Tesoro de EEUU, Scott Bessent, ofrecerá una rueda de prensa el lunes a las 1300 hora de Washington D.C. (1700 GMT), en medio de promesas de revelar medidas aún más severas contra un país que ha soportado sanciones económicas casi continuas desde la Revolución Islámica de 1979. "Al amanecer comienza un Día D económico: la mayor ofensiva financiera jamás lanzada contra un adversario", escribió Bessent en un artículo de opinión publicado el domingo en el Financial Times. Los países en conflicto llevan semanas sin lanzar ataques militares entre sí, pero tampoco han entablado conversaciones significativas para poner fin al conflicto, que ya dura seis meses. Miles de personas han perdido la vida, la mayoría de ellas en Irán y Líbano, desde que Estados Unidos e Israel iniciaron los ataques el 28 de febrero, lo que ha mermado gran parte de la capacidad militar convencional de Irán y le ha infligido un duro golpe económico, además de causar la muerte del líder supremo iraní, el ayatolá Alí Jamenei. Sin embargo, Irán ha conservado suficiente capacidad en materia de misiles y drones como para atacar a sus vecinos del golfo Pérsico y amenazar a los petroleros en el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que ha provocado que el tráfico marítimo en esta vía navegable clave quedara prácticamente paralizado y ha ejercido presión sobre los precios mundiales del combustible. Se desconoce la situación exacta del programa nuclear iraní, que los estadounidenses y los israelíes pretenden eliminar por completo. Sin detallar medidas concretas, Bessent señaló que EEUU apuntaría contra las "naciones temerosas" que practican la "política de apaciguamiento" al relacionarse con la economía y el sistema financiero iraníes. "Harían bien en considerar las consecuencias de mantener esa actitud", escribió en el Financial Times. Irán lleva días preparándose para las sanciones, emitiendo una serie de comunicados en tono enérgico que insinúan una respuesta militar de gran envergadura. Mohsen Rezaei, secretario del Consejo Supremo de Seguridad Nacional de Irán, sugirió el domingo una represalia económica. "Si la guerra económica continúa, no se exportará ni una sola gota de petróleo, ni a través del estrecho de Ormuz ni desde ningún lugar del golfo Pérsico", escribió Rezaei en una publicación en las redes sociales. "Irán considerará la participación o el apoyo de cualquier país a la guerra económica de Estados Unidos contra el pueblo iraní como un acto de guerra". Bessent había instado previamente a China a cooperar con EEUU, señalando que, históricamente, China ha obtenido la mitad de sus importaciones de petróleo de la región del golfo Pérsico. Un portavoz de la embajada de China en Washington respondió con una declaración en la que afirmaba que "las sanciones y la presión no ayudan a resolver el problema", al tiempo que abogaba por la vía diplomática. La economía iraní ya se encontraba bajo presión debido a las sanciones internacionales antes de que los ataques de EEUU e Israel destruyeran parte de su infraestructura. Aunque Teherán sigue mostrándose desafiante en apariencia, las autoridades iraníes han advertido de que nuevas medidas económicas punitivas podrían agravar las dificultades, reavivar los disturbios y erosionar aún más la legitimidad de la República Islámica. Irán entró en la guerra con una elevada inflación, una moneda debilitada, escasez energética, sanciones y profundas debilidades estructurales, y ahora debe hacer frente a una infraestructura dañada, un comercio interrumpido, la pérdida de producción y el costo de la reconstrucción. A falta de conversaciones oficiales presenciales entre EEUU e Irán —las últimas se celebraron en junio en Suiza—, otros países, como Qatar, Pakistán y Turquía, han intentado impulsar la vía diplomática. Irán dijo que el jefe del ejército pakistaní, Asim Munir, visitará Teherán el lunes como parte de los esfuerzos por restablecer la paz y la seguridad en la región, pero dio pocos detalles. Pakistán ha estado mediando en el conflicto y una fuente del Gobierno pakistaní dijo que Munir abordaría los últimos acontecimientos, incluida la amenaza de Estados Unidos de imponer nuevas sanciones. Los ataques de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán y los ataques israelíes contra Líbano durante la guerra han causado miles de muertos y millones de desplazados. Estados Unidos informó de que 18 militares habían perdido la vida y más de 750 habían resultado heridos.

item.title: Russia's Ozon says four logistics hubs targeted by Ukrainian drones
item.description: Four logistics hubs owned by Russia's second-largest online retailer Ozon in southern Russia were targeted in Ukrainian drone attacks, the company said on Monday, bringing the number of targeted facilities to six since August 22.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Four logistics hubs owned by Russia's second-largest online retailer Ozon in southern Russia were targeted in Ukrainian drone attacks, the company said on Monday, bringing the number of targeted facilities to six since August 22. Ozon said its logistics hub in Makhachkala, Dagestan, was on fire after a drone attack, while workers at warehouses in Adygeysk, in the Adygeya region, and Nevinnomyssk, in the Stavropol region, had been evacuated. "According to preliminary information, several people were injured," Ozon said in a statement, referring to the facility in Makhachkala, which had halted operations. The company also said a large fire broke out at its facility in the town of Enem in the Krasnodar region. It added that facilities in Adygeya and Stavropol were not damaged. Shares in Ozon fell by as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange on news of the attack, while shares in its major shareholder, private equity firm AFK Sistema, fell by almost 13%. Ozon has become Russia's second e-commerce giant, after rival Wildberries, to be targeted in Ukrainian drone attacks. Work at a logistics centre in the Samara region was halted after the first Ukrainian strike on the company's facilities on August 22.

item.title: Trump's Kim gambit deepens doubts over US reliability at a key moment for Asia
item.description: Donald Trump's olive branch to North Korea's Kim Jong Un at the expense of a long-standing ally comes at a pivotal moment for U.S. security ties in Asia, as partners from Japan to India reassess how much they can rely on Washington.
item.dc:creator: John Geddie, Yukiko Toyoda, Ben Blanchard, Aftab Ahmed
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump's olive branch to North Korea's Kim Jong Un at the expense of a long-standing ally comes at a pivotal moment for U.S. security ties in Asia, as partners from Japan to India reassess how much they can rely on Washington. The U.S. president's abrupt decision to [USN:L1N44D05G TEXT:"cut back"] military drills with South Korea last week, which he described as hostile to Pyongyang, has reinforced fears that Trump's unpredictability could strain alliances that have long maintained peace in the region, government officials and security experts said. Japan worries it too could find itself in Trump's cross-hairs as it embarks on thorny security negotiations; Taiwan is warily watching an upcoming summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping; and India is growing less certain of its place in Washington's strategic calculus. "The decision will certainly fuel growing doubts in the region about U.S. security commitments," said Jeremy Chan, a senior analyst with political risk consultancy Eurasia Group and former U.S. diplomat in Japan and China. Adding to the anxiety, the United States [USN:L6N44L07Y TEXT:"cancelled"] another military exercise with South Korea scheduled for next month, Seoul said on Monday, after Washington cited constraints on U.S. forces due to the Iran war. Trump has been frustrated by the failure of U.S. allies to support the war and made it clear that many of them must spend more on their own defence, a White House official said when asked about such concerns. He is [USN:L4N44H048 TEXT:"eager to restart talks"] with North Korea and secure a win on the international stage to counter his unpopular conflict with Iran, according to a person briefed on discussions between U.S. and South Korean officials. 'EXTREMELY TROUBLING' FOR TOKYO Trump's push to meet Kim - which has so far drawn a [USN:L4N44H048 TEXT:"frosty response"] from Pyongyang - could backfire and embolden nuclear-armed North Korea, said Itsunori Onodera, an influential Japanese lawmaker and former defence minister. Such a prospect is "extremely troubling" for Tokyo, he said on a Fuji TV news programme last Thursday. Despite Trump's overtures, Pyongyang [USN:L1N44H09Z TEXT:"fired a volley"] of ballistic missiles off its east coast earlier that day, triggering alerts in neighbouring South Korea and Japan. What worries Japanese officials more is Trump's approach as Tokyo embarks on talks with Washington over how much it should pay towards the cost of hosting U.S. forces, America's largest overseas deployment. Japan is bracing for the possibility that Trump could, with little warning, demand a sharp hike that would be politically difficult to swallow, said a senior Japanese government official, requesting anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter. Trump could also wield upcoming U.S. military exercises with Japan in October as leverage, analysts say. Officials in Washington and Tokyo said they did not expect the exercises to be curtailed, though Trump could change his mind at any point, they cautioned. The drills, known as Keen Sword, may already be smaller than their 2024 iteration because of the diversion of U.S. assets and personnel to the conflict with Iran. That shift - which recently saw America's only forward-deployed aircraft carrier in Asia, the USS George Washington, depart for the Middle East to relieve the beleaguered USS Abraham Lincoln - has stirred concern that U.S. deterrence against China [USN:L1N3ZR088 TEXT:"is being eroded"]. During a visit to Asia this month, Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby said working with allies to ensure combat readiness along the so-called first island chain that runs from Japan through the Philippines is a priority for Washington. TRUMP, XI AND TAIWAN Nowhere are concerns about China's growing military pressure more acute than in Taiwan, the democratically governed island claimed by Beijing. Trump has held up approval of a $14 billion package of arms sales to Taipei in order to maintain warm relations and a fragile trade truce with China's Xi. As Trump prepares for his latest round of summitry with Xi in Washington next month, officials in Taipei say they expect Washington will at the very least carve up the arms sales into smaller chunks to try and avoid upsetting Beijing too much. Domingo Yang of the Taiwan defence ministry's think tank, the Institute for National Defence and Security Research, says there is a distinction between Trump's rhetoric and actual U.S. behaviour, noting U.S. intelligence sharing, training and patrols with Taiwan remain substantial. A U.S. Navy aircraft [USN:L1N44J00A TEXT:"transited the Taiwan Strait"] on Friday in a move the United States described as demonstrating its "commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific." Trump's latest actions have also rocked confidence in India, where the U.S. risks squandering years of efforts to draw New Delhi closer as a counterweight to Russia and China, security analysts say. It also comes after the Pentagon's decision in June to rename its Asia military headquarters to Pacific Command from Indo-Pacific Command, a move some analysts say is a sign India is no longer as strategically important to Washington. The Pentagon denied any such shift. But Trump's steep tariffs on Indian exports and repeated claims that he had mediated an India-Pakistan ceasefire had already exasperated New Delhi. Officials there are now "very, very cautious" about committing to long-term defence deals with Washington, according to two Indian sources with knowledge of the matter. "The latest decision only reinforces President Trump's transactional view of foreign affairs and serves as a reminder that differences over specific policies, even among allies, can carry costs for the broader bilateral relationship," said Pearl Pandya, senior analyst at Armed Conflict Location & Event Data, a conflict monitoring group.

item.title: US refiners face historic stress test as global crisis looms
item.description: U.S. refineries have operated near maximum capacity for the longest sustained period in over a quarter century, scrambling to capture windfall profits created by the Iran war. But history offers a cautionary tale: “Super refining” runs that push plants too hard can cause major failures.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: U.S. refineries have operated near maximum capacity for the longest sustained period in over a quarter century, scrambling to capture windfall profits created by the [USN:L8N44H1WH TEXT:"Iran war"]. But history offers a cautionary tale: “Super refining” runs that push plants too hard can cause major failures. This has global implications. U.S. refineries’ ability to sustain today’s elevated operating rates for months, or potentially years, could mean the difference between an exceptionally tight global fuel market and a full-blown supply crisis marked by acute shortages, demand destruction and widespread economic pain. A U.S.-Israeli air campaign against Iran in late February triggered the closure of the [USN:L6N44E0UW TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"], [USN:L4N44I05C TEXT:"disrupting"] a fifth of global oil supply and severely hampering refining operations, particularly in Asia. Meanwhile, relentless Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries caused Moscow to suspend diesel exports in July. The result has been [USN:L6N44G0ZC TEXT:"a collapse"] in global fuel production. Global refinery throughput in July fell to 81 million barrels per day (bpd), nearly 5 million bpd, or about 6%, below the level at this point last year, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). The U.S., the world's largest crude producer and second-largest refiner after China, responded by ramping up exports of [USN:L1N41C0XB TEXT:"crude"], [USN:L1N40K11P TEXT:"gasoline, diesel and jet fuel"] to record levels, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), helping avert a truly cataclysmic supply shock. For the U.S. refining industry, the past six months have been an unprecedented bonanza. Benchmark margins for converting crude into transportation fuels have averaged more than $50 a barrel since the start of the war, more than double their 10-year average. As a result, major U.S. refiners including [USN:L4N43W0YL TEXT:"Valero"] (VLO.N) , [USN:L4N442125 TEXT:"Phillips 66"] (PSX.N) , [USN:L4N4410TR TEXT:"Marathon Petroleum"] (MPC.N) and [USN:L6N43Q18H TEXT:"Exxon Mobil"] (XOM.N) posted record or near-record second-quarter earnings. To generate those bumper profits, many companies postponed planned maintenance and kept plants running at full tilt. U.S. refinery throughput has averaged around 17 million bpd since the start of the conflict, significantly above its five-year average. The question now is how long this can last before something breaks. PARTY LIKE IT’S 1997 This period of sustained maximum production has few precedents in modern history. Over the past 11 weeks, U.S. refinery utilisation rates have hovered above 95% — a sustained level not seen in more than 25 years. In fact, refineries have only achieved such prolonged rates three times, based on EIA data going back to 1990. The closest parallels came in 1997 and 1998, when U.S. refineries recorded two separate 24-week stretches of utilisation rates above 95% — first between May and October 1997 and again between April and September 1998. In the summer of 1998, the refinery fleet exceeded 100% utilisation – the only time this has occurred in EIA records. That extraordinary performance was driven by a rare combination of low crude prices and consistently strong fuel demand, giving refiners every incentive to keep operations running flat out. A similar episode followed in 2000, when refineries operated above 95% utilisation for 13 consecutive weeks, but the conditions were markedly different. The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries had introduced production cuts in 1999 that caused crude prices to nearly double by mid-2000. While this squeezed refinery profit margins, it coincided with the early stages of the China-driven commodities super-cycle, when global fuel demand skyrocketed, forcing refineries to run hard to meet it. The rally ultimately ended as crude became too expensive to sustain such high operating rates. The current episode looks quite different from any of these precedents. Today's utilisation surge is being driven not by cheap feedstock or runaway demand but by a severe shortage of refining capacity caused by war-related damage in Iran and Russia. But those episodes illustrate the risk refiners are taking. A DANGEROUS PRECIPICE Running complex refining systems at breakneck speeds for extended periods inevitably increases the risk of equipment failures, accidents and unplanned outages. Faced with soaring margins and a global fuel shortage, many U.S. refiners have deferred essential maintenance originally scheduled for the second quarter, pushing much of the work into late 2026 or even 2027. The risk is that doing this could ultimately lead to sharp, unplanned capacity losses. History offers mixed lessons. The first super-refining episode in 1997 ended relatively gradually, with utilisation easing from above 95% in mid-October to around 92% a month later before quickly rebounding. The reckoning came the following year. After the 24-week run in 1998, utilisation plunged from around 95% in late September to 86% by mid-October as several refineries were forced into emergency maintenance after months of operating at full capacity. A similar pattern emerged in 2018, when an eight-week period of utilisation above 95% was followed by a rapid drop to 89% within weeks. The 2000 rally was the notable exception, as it ended without a comparable collapse. So what’s the risk of a breakdown this time? On the one hand, the industry today has a far better understanding of the risks associated with prolonged periods of elevated utilisation. Yet today’s global refining crisis is unlike anything refiners have ever faced. Fuel inventories are being depleted, while severe damage to refining infrastructure in the Middle East and Russia is likely to leave the world with reduced processing capacity for years. The risk of losing further capacity is greater than at any time in the recent past because global refining output is nearly 2 million bpd below demand, according to the IEA. That creates a dangerous dilemma. The longer refining margins remain elevated, the greater the temptation for refiners to keep running flat out. But the harder they run, the greater the risk of failures that could remove even more fuel from an already stretched market. For now, America's refiners are serving as the world's supplier of last resort. The danger is that the world has become so dependent on them that even a small disruption to their operations could tip an already fragile market into a genuine fuel crisis. (The opinions expressed here are those of Ron Bousso , a columnist for Reuters.) Enjoying this column? item.title: US LNG exports set for endurance test as high gas prices bite
item.description: U.S. LNG producers have shipped out record volumes of the super-chilled fuel so far in 2026, but rising global natural gas prices may soon curb demand from cost-sensitive buyers.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Maguire
item.content:encoded: U.S. LNG producers have shipped out record volumes of the super-chilled fuel so far in 2026, but rising global natural gas prices may soon curb demand from cost-sensitive buyers. Key forward gas and LNG prices in Europe and Asia — which together account for over 80% of U.S. LNG shipments — have climbed to their highest in more than three years, data from LSEG shows. The ongoing U.S. and Israeli war with Iran has disrupted freight traffic in the Gulf and cut LNG flows from key exporter Qatar by over 60% from the year before, according to Kpler, opening the door to higher prices and record U.S. cargoes. However, while reduced Qatari shipments have tightened markets, exporters may soon face softer demand as high cargo costs and a seasonal slowdown in gas consumption prompt buyers to delay purchases. PRICED OUT Estimated forward prices for LNG deliveries to Asia are set to climb to above $22 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) for October, November and December delivery, according to LSEG. That compares to an average of just under $17 per MMBtu for 2026 so far, and would be the highest seen in Asia since the start of 2023 when global gas markets were reeling from Russia's invasion of Ukraine and disruptions to Russian gas flows. Given that gas consumption in Asia tends to drop after summer — as demand for cooling systems eases — gas purchases by major consumers in Japan, China and South Korea are likely to soften until utilities move to restock as winter kicks in. In Europe, gas consumers are expected to face benchmark natural gas prices in the Netherlands gas trading hub of around $21.50 to $22.50 per MMBtu over the October to December period, which would be the highest since late 2022, LSEG data shows. Those elevated prices come as Europe's gas demand shows signs of softening. Expanding renewable electricity generation is [USN:L1N44A004 TEXT:"displacing gas-fired power output"], while households and businesses are increasingly electrifying heating and other energy uses in an effort to reduce fossil fuel consumption. At the same time, European gas inventories remain well below the long-term average, meaning utilities will need to replenish stockpiles before heating demand picks up. However, recent import trends suggest buyers are in no rush to secure additional LNG at current prices. Europe imported a total of 6.2 million metric tons of LNG in July, according to Kpler, the lowest July total since 2021. That slow import pace suggests buyer concerns over fuel costs currently outweigh worries about potential supply security. EXPORTER PERSPECTIVE For U.S. LNG sellers, the prospect of a near-term lull in importer demand will not be much of a concern, especially with record tallies already recorded for the first seven months of the year. U.S. firms exported just over 73 million tons of LNG from January through July, which is up 23% from the same months in 2025, Kpler data shows. But prolonged periods of high gas prices in key target markets may accelerate electrification efforts and the shift to alternative power sources. This is especially likely in cost-sensitive markets in Asia which are also home to rapidly expanding renewables generation and strong growth in battery storage systems. High natural gas prices may also serve to discourage discretionary purchases by storage operators, who will be wary of refilling tanks while prices are high in case demand stays weak through winter and limits reselling opportunities. LNG exporters will also be mindful of planned steep increases in export volumes, with several liquefaction expansions expected in the U.S. and Canada alone before the end of the decade. Most of those planned expansion projects were greenlit on the assumption that global gas consumption will continue to expand in line with supply, in every market. But if gas prices in key regions remain high enough to curb local demand and accelerate energy transition efforts, exporters may soon face serious competition when it comes to finding willing buyers, regardless of how much they may have to sell. The opinions expressed here are those of the author , a columnist for Reuters. Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. item.title: US cancels joint marine drills with South Korea over Iran war-related force constraints
item.description: The United States cancelled a joint amphibious landing drill scheduled for next month with South Korea, Seoul's Marine Corps said on Monday, after Washington cited constraints on the availability of U.S. forces due to the war in Iran.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States cancelled a joint amphibious landing drill scheduled for next month with South Korea, Seoul's Marine Corps said on Monday, after Washington cited constraints on the availability of U.S. forces due to the war in Iran. The U.S. Marine Corps formally notified its South Korean counterpart in June that force availability would be constrained for the division-level exercise, known as Ssangyong , a South Korean Marine Corps spokesperson told a press briefing. The allies remain in close consultations on resuming the drills, the spokesperson said. He did not specify what measures might be taken to prevent future cancellations or to make up for lost training opportunities. U.S. Forces Korea did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The cancellation follows U.S. President Donald Trump's surprise order to scale back a separate annual joint military exercise that ended last Friday, citing the cost and Seoul's refusal to take part in the Iran war. Trump also wrote on his Truth Social platform that the [USN:L1N44D05G TEXT:"Ulchi Freedom Shield drills"] sent "a signal that was totally inappropriate and hostile, to a Country that, as long as Donald J. Trump has been President, has been unthreatening and respectful." Despite the reduction of the exercises, Pyongyang [USN:L1N44H09Z TEXT:"fired "]10 short-range ballistic missiles last week and issued a [USN:FWN44H0SM TEXT:"statement "]denouncing the exercises. North Korea has long condemned such joint exercises as rehearsals for invasion.

item.title: ｢公邸も職場｣､高市首相がSNSで外出控える理由を自己弁護－SP負担軽減
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 高市早苗首相は、公務で外出する必要がない限り公邸にとどまる自身の行動について、SNSを通じて理解を求めた。職員に過度な負担をかけずに、長時間働くことができるためだと説明している。

高市首相は22日のX（旧ツイッター）への投稿で、「公邸内での打合せなど公邸での執務は、総理の日々の動静としては報じられませんが、私としては、『公邸も職場』というのが実感です」と記した。

2025年10月の首相就任以降、高市氏は昼夜を問わず働くスタイルや、公邸で資料を読み込む習慣で知られている。7月には、「0時間～3時間睡眠が常態化」と投稿した。

日本経済新聞は21日、高市氏が首相に就任して以降の土日・祝日の過ごし方を分析した結果、5割超は公邸や議員宿舎で終日過ごしていたと報じた。過去3人の首相は、休日に宿舎や公邸から出なかった日は3－16%にとどまっていたという。

高市氏はXで、公邸にとどまって執務する理由を強調。「官邸と公邸、どちらでもしっかりと仕事ができる環境をつくってきました」と説明した。

一連の投稿からは、1人で仕事に打ち込むことを重視する姿勢と、自身の考えを伝えるためにSNSを頻繁に活用する姿勢の両方がうかがえる。

7月までの首相のスケジュールをブルームバーグ・ニュースが分析したところ、財務省当局者との面会は前任の首相2人よりも50%少なく、閣僚会議の開催回数も過去14年間の首相で最も少なかった。

高市氏は歴代首相に比べてメディアに直接語る機会が少なく、代わりにXへ投稿することを好む。有権者に直接訴えかける姿勢や、意思決定に時間をかける一部の歴代首相の合意形成重視のスタイルとは対照的な高市氏の姿勢が、2月の衆院選で歴史的な圧勝を収める一因となった。

一方、こうした一匹おおかみ的なスタイルは、一部の野党議員やメディアに登場するコメンテーターから批判を招いており、公邸にとどまることを好む点を問題視する声もある。世論調査では、高市内閣の支持率が低下しており、物価高への対応という国民生活の切実な課題からずれた法案の成立を優先しているとの批判も出ている。

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe indécise avant une semaine chargée, focus sur le Moyen-Orient et Nvidia (actualisé)
item.description: Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues sur une note hésitante lundi à l'ouverture, les investisseurs faisant preuve de prudence en ce début de semaine riche en événements géopolitiques et en données macroéconomiques, sans parler des résultats attendus du géant des puces électroniques Nvidia et du symposium de Jackson Hole.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues sur une note hésitante lundi à l'ouverture, les investisseurs faisant preuve de prudence en ce début de semaine riche en événements géopolitiques et en données macroéconomiques, sans parler des résultats attendus du géant des puces électroniques Nvidia et du symposium de Jackson Hole. Les contrats à terme sur indices suggèrent une ouverture baisse de 0,07% pour le CAC 40 parisien (.FCHI) et de 0,16% pour le Dax à Francfort (.GDAXI) . Le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) est attendu stable et le FTSE de la Bourse de Londres pourrait prendre 0,15%. La confiance des investisseurs devrait rester modérée ce lundi, les négociations de paix au Moyen-Orient demeurant dans l'impasse, ce qui met les marchés pétroliers sous tension et a entraîné une hausse de 5% des prix du pétrole au cours de la semaine dernière. La retenue s'impose d'autant plus dans le contexte d'une nouvelle escalade verbale entre les États-Unis et l'Iran. Washington a fait part vendredi de son intention d'infliger à la République islamique "les plus sévères sanctions de son histoire", selon les termes du secrétaire au Trésor Scott Bessent, qui doit détailler ces mesures lundi à 14h00 heure de Washington (18h00 GMT). "On ne sait pas encore si la politique américaine visant à isoler économiquement l'Iran s'avérera efficace", écrit dans une note Vivek Dhar, analyste spécialisé dans les matières premières à la Commonwealth Bank of Australia. "Mais si les mesures américaines produisent les effets escomptés, la capacité de l'Iran à riposter par une escalade de la violence deviendra un risque croissant dont les marchés de l'énergie devront tenir compte". Le chef de l'armée pakistanaise, Asim Munir, [USN:L8N44K01M TEXT:"se rendra"] lundi à Téhéran dans le cadre des efforts de médiation d'Islamabad dans le conflit entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran, a déclaré dimanche le porte-parole du ministère iranien des Affaires étrangères. Le ministre des Affaires étrangères d'Oman se rendra pour sa part mardi à Téhéran afin de poursuivre ses discussions avec l'Iran concernant le détroit d'Ormuz, selon le porte-parole du ministère. Les négociations entre Oman et l'Iran sur Ormuz ont déjà suscité la colère des États-Unis ces dernières semaines. Les opérateurs espèrent également obtenir des éclaircissements sur les perspectives des taux d'intérêt américains ou sur les turbulences du marché obligataire lorsque le président de la Réserve fédérale (Fed), Kevin Warsh, prendra la parole vendredi à Jackson Hole, dans le Wyoming, même si sa réticence à donner des indications prospectives laisse craindre des déclarations plutôt prudentes. Les chiffres de l'inflation PCE aux États-Unis, l'indicateur privilégié par la Fed pour fixer ses taux, seront aussi publiés cette semaine et pourraient encore influencer les anticipations du marché concernant la réunion de septembre, qui estiment à 40% la probabilité d'une hausse des coûts d'emprunt. Les marchés observeront également avec attention la publication des résultats trimestriels de plusieurs géants de la tech, notamment ceux de Nvidia (NVDA.O) mercredi. "Ces dernières années, les résultats financiers de Nvidia ont souvent constitué à eux seuls un événement macroéconomique majeur, suscitant des réactions comparables à celles provoquées par les rapports sur l'emploi aux États-Unis et les chiffres de l'IPC", écrivent les analystes de Deutsche Bank. "Cependant, au cours des derniers trimestres, les surprises positives en matière de résultats n'ont pas été aussi importantes que celles observées en 2023-2024, et à l'issue de chacune des quatre dernières publications de résultats, le cours de l'action Nvidia a en réalité baissé le lendemain", ajoutent-ils. LES VALEURS A SUIVRE : [USN:L8N44I0XK] A WALL STREET La Bourse de New York a fini dans le vert vendredi mais enregistre des pertes hebdomadaires, les turbulences sur le marché obligataire et les tensions géopolitiques freinant l'appétit pour le risque. L'indice Dow Jones (.DJI) a gagné 0,98%, le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) , plus large, a pris 0,43%, et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) a avancé de son côté de 0,44%. EN ASIE L'indice Nikkei (.N225) de la Bourse de Tokyo a perdu 0,74%, affecté par la prudence entourant les valeurs liées à l'intelligence artificielle (IA) avant les résultats de Nvidia. Le marché japonais est également pénalisé par les craintes liées à l'inflation : les investisseurs et analystes s'attendent à ce que la Banque du Japon (BoJ) relève ses taux d'intérêt le mois prochain lors de sa prochaine réunion de politique monétaire. Le Kospi (.KS11) a reculé de 3,12%, Samsung (005930.KS) abandonnant 8,7%. Les investisseurs se montrent déçus par le plan de redistribution aux actionnaires annoncé par le géant des puces, car ils espéraient notamment bénéficier d'une part plus importante des excédents de trésorerie générés par l'IA. En Chine, l'indice composite de la Bourse de Shanghai (.SSEC) perd 0,96% et le CSI 300 (.CSI300) des grandes capitalisations abandonne 1,59%, pénalisés par une émission surprise d'actions d'Alibaba (9988.HK) (-9,27%) avec une décote de 8,4% par rapport à son cours de clôture de vendredi. Il s'agit de la plus importante offre publique secondaire jamais réalisée à Hong Kong, destinée à financer les projets de développement du géant du commerce en ligne dans le domaine de l'IA . "L'ADN d'Alibaba réside dans le commerce électronique, et non dans les technologies de pointe", déclare Yang Tingwu, directeur général adjoint de la société de gestion d'actifs Tongheng Investment. "Peu importe le montant qu'elle investisse dans le matériel d'IA, elle risque fort d'être devancée par ses concurrents en matière d'innovation technologique", ajoute-t-il. La Bourse de Hong Kong (.HSI) cède 2,08%. Le groupe de "fast fashion" Shein a par ailleurs [USN:L6N44L01T TEXT:"confirmé"] lundi son intention d'entrer en Bourse à Hong Kong le 1er septembre. TAUX / CHANGES Les rendements obligataires sont en légère baisse lundi, même si le plan du Trésor américain visant à doubler le montant de ses rachats de dette à long terme n'a pas eu d'effets significatifs, dans un contexte de hausse générale des coûts de financement des principales économies mondiales. Le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans perd 3,2 points de base à 4,7060%. Le deux ans recule de près de 1 point de base à 4,2252%. Dans la zone euro, le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans cède 1,5 point de base à 3,2415%. Le deux ans est également en légère baisse et ressort à 2,8232%. Sur le marché des changes, le dollar grappille 0,06% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , tout en se situant près de ses plus bas niveaux de ces derniers mois, sur un marché déstabilisé par la promesse du Trésor américain de racheter davantage d'obligations. L'euro est quasi stable (-0,03%) à 1,1676 dollar . PÉTROLE Les cours du pétrole reculent lundi, les investisseurs prenant leurs bénéfices avant des détails sur les nouvelles sanctions américains contre l'Iran, susceptibles de perturber davantage l'approvisionnement en provenance du Moyen-Orient. Le Brent perd 1,63% à 92,85 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) 1,99% à 85,33 dollars. AUCUN INDICATEUR ÉCONOMIQUE MAJEUR À L'AGENDA DU 24 AOÛT

item.title: Chinese research institute apologises after sparking alarm with 7.7 quake alert
item.description: A Chinese research institute located in the southwestern Chinese metropolis of Chengdu apologised on Monday for initially issuing a higher magnitude earthquake than what other monitors said occurred, sparking some panic among people.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Chinese research institute located in the southwestern Chinese metropolis of Chengdu apologised on Monday for initially issuing a higher magnitude earthquake than what other monitors said occurred, sparking some panic among people. China's Earthquake Networks Center said a 4.7 magnitude earthquake struck Yibin in southwest China's Sichuan province at 8:26 a.m. (0026 GMT) on Monday. However, the Institute of Care-Life, a Chengdu-based disaster reduction laboratory, issued a 7.7 magnitude earthquake alert just five seconds after the quake struck. Addressing the significant discrepancy, it said that the network revised the estimate lower to 6.4 at the sixth second, 3.7 at the seventh second, 4.1 at the eighth second and 3.9 at the 16th second. The Institute of Care-Life said it will investigate the cause for the deviation as soon as possible to improve its services. The false alert caused panic among many users, state-backed newspaper the Global Times said.

item.title: China's netizens rage against professor who said gig work was a type of 'welfare'
item.description: The term "flexible employment" has gone viral in China after a prominent economics professor described gig work as a form of "welfare", drawing widespread public anger and highlighting deep anxieties over job insecurity.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The term "flexible employment" has gone viral in China after a prominent economics professor described gig work as a form of "welfare", drawing widespread public anger and highlighting deep anxieties over job insecurity. Zhang Dandan, a professor of economics and deputy dean at Peking University's National School of Development, made the remarks during a discussion on social protection for gig workers, on the popular financial show "Let's Talk" last week. She argued that from the perspective of labour economics, "flexibility itself is a form of welfare." While regular employees trade schedule flexibility for pensions and other benefits, flexible workers enjoy greater control over their time at the cost of weaker social protections, Zhang said. The comments triggered a fierce backlash over the weekend, with social media users accusing Zhang of being oblivious to the harsh realities of the gig economy. Zhang did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. The controversy has struck a nerve for many in China, where a cooling economy has made secure, full-time employment harder to find. The China New Employment Forms Research Center, a think tank, estimates the number of flexible workers — those without permanent full-time contracts — will rise to 320 million this year from 280 million in 2025. That represents about 44% of China's urban workforce and is roughly equivalent to the entire population of the United States. 'RUBBING SALT INTO WOUNDS' The rise of gig jobs in China, where employers are not mandated to make social insurance contributions, heightens long-term [USN:L8N42I0IK TEXT:"risks"] for China's already strained welfare and pension systems, some industry experts have warned. Prominent nationalist commentator Hu Xijin, a former editor at the state-backed Global Times newspaper, called Zhang's remarks "shocking" and "unacceptable." "She has paid the price for her reputation for speaking this way, and the responsibility lies with her," Hu wrote on his Weibo account, adding that she should "respond to public opinion, explain where necessary, and apologize where appropriate." Despite the backlash, some social media users pointed out Zhang's academic career had focused largely on documenting the struggles of gig workers and advocating for their social security. Zhang noted last year that on-demand workers made up about 31% of the workforce in China's manufacturing sector. During peak seasons, that proportion can rise to as high as 80% for large manufacturers with more than 10,000 workers, she said. Nevertheless, Zhang's framing of "flexibility" as a benefit was seen as insensitive. "Such comments from experts are no less than rubbing salt into the wounds of those without job security," one Weibo user wrote. Another user pointed out the relentless pressure faced by delivery drivers and couriers: "Every day, they are racing against the platform's algorithm at all costs, without rest... [flexible work] is precisely the most unavoidable of choices, not a preference."

item.title: China's netizens rage against professor who said gig work was a type of 'welfare' - Reuters

item.title: Dax kaum verändert erwartet - Geo- und Handelspolitik im Blick
item.description: Der Dax wird am Montag der Kursentwicklung an den Terminmärkten zufolge mit wenig Bewegung in den Handel starten. Am Freitag war er um 0,6 Prozent gestiegen und schloss bei 26.136 Punkten. Auch die wichtigsten US-Indizes schlugen nach einer schwachen Börsenwoche einen Erholungskurs ein. Sorgen über ausufernde Staatsfinanzen, die anhaltend hohen Ölpreise und der Renditeanstieg am Anleihenmarkt begrenzten jedoch die Kursgewinne.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
Der Dax (.GDAXI) wird am Montag der Kursentwicklung an den Terminmärkten zufolge mit wenig Bewegung in den Handel starten. Am [USN:L8N44I0Z9 TEXT:"Freitag"] war er um 0,6 Prozent gestiegen und schloss bei 26.136 Punkten. Auch die wichtigsten [USN:L8N44I19H TEXT:"US-Indizes"] (.DJI) (.SPX) (.IXIC) schlugen nach einer schwachen Börsenwoche einen Erholungskurs ein. Sorgen über ausufernde Staatsfinanzen, die anhaltend hohen Ölpreise und der Renditeanstieg am Anleihenmarkt begrenzten jedoch die Kursgewinne. Am Montag blicken die Anleger erneut auf die Geopolitik. US-Finanzminister Scott Bessent hält ab 20.00 Uhr (MESZ) eine Pressekonferenz. Erwartet wird, dass er Einzelheiten zu den am Donnerstag [USN:L8N44H1O1 TEXT:"angekündigten"] "härtesten Sanktionen der Geschichte" gegen Iran nennt. Ziel dieser Sanktionen ist es, die iranische Regierung zum Zusammenbruch zu bringen. US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte allen Ländern mit wirtschaftlichen Konsequenzen gedroht, die dem Iran in irgendeiner Form helfen. Zum Wochenstart leiten zudem Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz, der französische Präsident Emmanuel Macron und der britische Premierminister Andy Burnham gemeinsam ein Treffen der sogenannten Koalition der Willigen zur Unterstützung der Ukraine. Im Fokus steht zudem die Handelspolitik. Nach dem [USN:L8N44J00Q TEXT:"gescheiterten"] Handelsabkommen und den neuen Zöllen der USA gegen Kanada kündigte die Regierung in Ottawa am Samstag [USN:L8N44J038 TEXT:"Gegenmaßnahmen"] an. item.title: Australia's bowlers restore order but batting headaches remain ahead of South Africa tour
item.description: Normal service resumed for Australia as their formidable bowling unit hit their marks in the second test against Bangladesh in Mackay but questions remain over a batting order that continues to misfire at the top.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: Normal service resumed for Australia as their formidable bowling unit hit their marks in the second test against Bangladesh in Mackay but questions remain over a batting order that continues to misfire at the top. Australia's [USN:L6N44K01P TEXT:"innings and 51-run "]victory was a strong comeback from the Darwin defeat as pace leaders Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins blasted away the tourists' batters in a timely reminder of their quality ahead of a tough, three-test tour of South Africa in October. Australia's batting has left selectors with a headache, though, and struggling number three Marnus Labuschagne may be nervous about his place in the squad for South Africa. South Africa-born Labuschagne was already under major scrutiny after two poor dismissals in Darwin before he was bowled for four in Mackay by Shoriful Islam, the ball catching his thigh pad before hitting the stumps. Upon his dismissal, Labuschagne gave the look of a man forsaken by the cricketing gods and later took scissors to his thigh pad in an unusual gear modification. But behind the theatrics was a batter who had strayed far across his crease and given Shoriful a look at leg stump, further evidence for pundits of a need for change. "There's some technical deficiency there, but he's making the margin for error for the bowlers too great," said former Australia captain Ricky Ponting. "It's well and truly time to have a look at somebody else." Labuschagne's exit would be the second top-order batter dropped in two matches after opener Jake Weatherald was dumped in the wake of the fiasco in Darwin, where Australia fell to a shock nine-wicket defeat. Weatherald's replacement Matt Renshaw hardly inspired in his first test in over three years, falling for eight with a nick to the slips, but he will be afforded time to bed into the role. Whether Travis Head should accompany him at the top of the order remains a troublesome question for selectors. Moved up from the middle order for the Ashes as Usman Khawaja struggled with injury, Head has remained there despite not really being seen as a proper opener. Some former players, including Mark Waugh, want Head back down in the middle order but that would mean gambling with two unproven openers against South Africa, who beat Australia for the World Test Championship title last year. With runs in Darwin and Mackay, Cameron Green has belatedly shored up his spot at number five so bringing Head back down would mean upsetting the formula of having wicketkeeper Alex Carey at six and the second all-rounder Beau Webster at seven. Selectors picked a thin 13-man squad for the Bangladesh series but are expected to take at least 16 to South Africa and include additional batting cover. Quite who gets the nod among the batters on the fringes is far from certain, with no real stand-out candidates having emerged. Carey said there was no urgency to shake up Australia's batting lineup further. "I think we felt a little bit like we left some runs out there (against Bangladesh), so we are always looking to improve as a batting unit," he told reporters in Mackay. "We are hungry. We are working really hard."

item.title: Norway asks supreme court to overturn environmental verdict against oilfields
item.description: Norway's government will on Monday ask the country's supreme court to overturn a ruling by lower-court judges that found three oilfield development permits invalid due to a lack of climate considerations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Norway's government will on Monday ask the country's supreme court to overturn a ruling by lower-court judges that found three oilfield development permits invalid due to a lack of climate considerations. The case pits environmental groups against Norway's oil industry, provider of half the country's export revenue, as well as the government whose policy is to [USN:L8N44I0B4 TEXT:"prolong the extraction"] of crude and natural gas for decades to come. Two lower courts have [USN:L8N3WQ1LQ TEXT:"ruled in favour"] of Greenpeace and Young Friends of the Earth since the two groups first brought the case to trial in 2023, finding that Norway failed to properly assess the environmental impact from the three fields. The case concerns Equinor's (EQNR.OL) Breidablikk and Aker BP's (AKRBP.OL) Tyrving and Yggdrasil fields, of which the first two are already in production while the third is due to come on stream next year. The green campaigners argue that the government failed to consider the climate impact of the burning of the fields' oil and gas, known as Scope 3 emissions, and that efforts to rectify this at a later stage were invalid. But the lower courts have declined to order a halt to production while the legal process is ongoing, and have also suggested that the government could seek to remedy regulatory shortcomings. "The state will argue that the additional assessments of foreign emissions now clearly satisfy all the requirements," the Office of the Attorney General said in a note to the court ahead of Monday's hearing. Norway produces around 2% of global oil and became Europe's largest supplier of natural gas after Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, making it a crucial provider of energy. The supreme court hearing is set to run for four days, and a verdict in the case is expected sometime later this year.

item.title: Arson and bomb attacks hit Thailand's deep south, authorities say
item.description: Suspected insurgents set fire to government buildings, shops, cars and utility poles in more than 70 locations across four of Thailand's southernmost provinces over the weekend, injuring at least three people in a coordinated series of arson attacks, authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Suspected insurgents set fire to government buildings, shops, cars and utility poles in more than 70 locations across four of Thailand's southernmost provinces over the weekend, injuring at least three people in a coordinated series of arson attacks, authorities said. More than 7,800 people have been killed in provinces bordering Malaysia since 2004, when the latest round of a long-running insurgency led mainly by the Barisan Revolusi Nasional (BRN) flared. Here are more details provided by Thai officials: There were at least 78 incidents across four provinces: 40 in Narathiwat, 21 in Yala, 15 in Pattani and two in Songkhla. No group has claimed responsibility. Most of the attacks took place on Saturday evening across Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat and parts of Songkhla, with some more on Sunday. A rail line was hit by explosives in Narathiwat, prompting the suspension of services in that section. Authorities have imposed a curfew in Narathiwat, and at a meeting on Sunday Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul asked the security forces to ensure public safety. Thailand's predominantly Muslim and ethnic Malay deep south has faced a decades-long insurgency seeking greater autonomy or independence. The region was part of the independent Malay sultanate of Patani before its incorporation into Thailand was formalised in 1909. The attacks come as Thailand seeks to revive peace talks with the BRN, the main separatist group fighting in the region. Chief negotiator Thanut Suvarnananda [USN:L4N4420WY TEXT:"told"] Reuters this month that Bangkok wanted to move beyond trading concessions for reduced violence and address political grievances, including governance. Malaysian-facilitated peace talks have repeatedly stalled since they began in 2013. Lieutenant General Norathip Poinok, who commands the Thai army in the southern region, told local media on Monday that authorities had received intelligence nearly two months ago warning of attacks on government buildings, shops and power infrastructure. Norathip described the attacks as retaliation for crackdowns on insurgents and illicit businesses, including drug and contraband trafficking, that fund militant groups.

item.title: Coach carrying German high-school students crashes in Netherlands
item.description: A coach carrying high-school students from Germany crashed in the east of the Netherlands early on Monday, injuring eight people, who were taken to hospital, Dutch police said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A coach carrying high-school students from Germany crashed in the east of the Netherlands early on Monday, injuring eight people, who were taken to hospital, Dutch police said. "Some of the victims taken to the hospital are seriously injured," the police department of Gelderland province said in a post on X. Other people suffered minor injuries in the accident. The coach, which carried more than 50 people, according to a police spokesperson, crashed near the town of Wezep, some 100 km (62 miles) east of Amsterdam around 4 a.m. (0200 GMT) due to a collision with a delivery van, whose driver was among the injured victims. The A28 highway was closed in both directions following the accident.

item.title: 猛暑のニッポン、暑さ対策に「脱毛」を選ぶ男たち 短パン普及が追い風
item.description:
日本の夏はますます暑さを増しており、男性たちは新たな「暑さ対策」に乗り出している。それは体毛をなくすことだ。
◇
年々、猛暑が厳しさを増す日本の夏。新たな暑さ対策として、脱毛を選ぶ男性が増えている。
利用者 「結構あったかいみたいな感じですね。痛みはほとんどなくて、当たってる部分だけあったかい」
施術を受けている24歳の男性は、脱毛で汗の量が減り、清潔に感じられると話した。
夏は男性向け美容クリニックの繁忙期で、予約が取りにくくなっている。
ゴリラクリニック銀座ANNEX院 太田博之院長 「（クリニックを）最初に立ち上げた頃、11年ほど前は、施術の枠が完全に埋まるということはそんなになかった。今は枠が埋まって、予約が取りにくくなるほど、お客様の数が増えている。クリニックの数も増やしたので、そう考えると（利用者数が）相当増えたという印象はある」
ショートパンツをはくことに抵抗を感じない人が増えていることも背景にある
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
日本の夏はますます暑さを増しており、男性たちは新たな「暑さ対策」に乗り出している。それは体毛をなくすことだ。

◇

年々、猛暑が厳しさを増す日本の夏。新たな暑さ対策として、脱毛を選ぶ男性が増えている。

利用者 「結構あったかいみたいな感じですね。痛みはほとんどなくて、当たってる部分だけあったかい」

施術を受けている24歳の男性は、脱毛で汗の量が減り、清潔に感じられると話した。

夏は男性向け美容クリニックの繁忙期で、予約が取りにくくなっている。

ゴリラクリニック銀座ANNEX院　太田博之院長 「（クリニックを）最初に立ち上げた頃、11年ほど前は、施術の枠が完全に埋まるということはそんなになかった。今は枠が埋まって、予約が取りにくくなるほど、お客様の数が増えている。クリニックの数も増やしたので、そう考えると（利用者数が）相当増えたという印象はある」

ショートパンツをはくことに抵抗を感じない人が増えていることも背景にある。かつてショートパンツは、子どもの服やビーチで着るものと見なされることが多かった。

日本最大級の美容予約・口コミサイトによると、調査対象の男性の4分の1超が過去1年間に下肢の脱毛を経験したという。

記録的な猛暑を受け、政府は今年、長年続けてきた「クールビズ」の取り組みを拡充した。ノーネクタイ・ノージャケットの服装で職員が涼しく働けるようにし、冷房に必要なエネルギーの削減を目指す。

item.title: South Africa telco MTN's half-year adjusted profit rises more than 21%
item.description: South African mobile operator MTN Group reported on Monday a 21.3% increase in half-year adjusted profit, largely driven by subscriber growth that accelerated in the second quarter, and double-digit growth in service revenue.
item.dc:creator: Nqobile Dludla
item.content:encoded: South African mobile operator MTN Group (MTNJ.J) reported on Monday a 21.3% increase in half-year adjusted profit, largely driven by subscriber growth that accelerated in the second quarter, and double-digit growth in service revenue. Africa's biggest telecom operator, which has more than 317 million customers in 19 markets, said its adjusted headline earnings per share (HEPS) rose to 793 cents in the six months ended June 30, up from 654 cents a year earlier. Here are the rest of the details: Reported HEPS declined by 5.8%, due to a non-cash impairment of its 49% stake in Irancell amid the Iran conflict and foreign exchange losses in South Sudan. Group service revenue, excluding the effect of currency fluctuations, grew 17.5% to 115.3 billion rand ($7.21 billion), led by strong performances in MTN Nigeria (MTNN.LG) , up 25.7%, MTN Ghana (MTNGH.GH) , up 32.3%, and growth in Cameroon, Uganda and Cote d'Ivoire. Despite competitive pressure on the prepaid market at MTN South Africa, service revenue growth edged up by 1.5%. Core earnings rose by 24.4% to 56 billion rand, while the EBITDA margin widened by 3.1 percentage points to 47.1%. ($1 = 15.9948 rand)

item.title: 中国向けイラン産原油、米封鎖でオファー減少 価格上昇＝関係筋
item.description:
Siyi Liu Chen Aizhu
[シンガポール ２１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Siyi Liu　Chen Aizhu

[シンガポール ２１日 ロイター] - 米国の封鎖によりイランからの出荷が減少する中、中国の買い手に対するイラン産原油のオファーが減少し、価格が上昇している。関係筋が明らかにした。

４人の貿易筋によると、９月と１０月渡しの中国向けイラン産原油のオファー数は、７月と８月渡しに比べて減少。船舶追跡会社ケプラーのデータによると、イランの原油輸出は７月中旬以降減少しており、それ以降、イラン産原油を積載した超大型タンカーがホルムズ海峡を通過した形跡は見られない。ただし、多くの船舶がトランスポンダー（船舶自動識別装置）をオフにしているため、追跡は困難となっている。

この供給不足は「ティーポット」と呼ばれる中国の独立系製油所を脅かしている。ティーポットは中国の精製能力の約５分の１を占めており、制裁対象の原油の最大の買い手となっている。

３人の貿易筋によると、通常はディスカウント価格で販売されるイラン産原油の一部が、ＩＣＥブレント先物に対してプレミアム付きでオファーされている。ある筋は、１バレル当たり約２ドルのプレミアムになっていると指摘。これは急激な変化であり、イラン産ライト原油の貨物は最近、１カ月前と同様に１バレル当たり約３ドルのディスカウント価格が提示されていた。

ケプラーのシニア原油アナリスト、ムーユー・シュー氏は、米封鎖海域外の海上貯蔵施設としてシンガポールの東側にあるマレーシア海域の船舶に４０００万バレルのイラン産原油が積載されていると推定しているが、その大部分はすでに買い手に引き渡されることが約束されていると指摘。２１日のリンクトイン投稿で「積載済みのイラン産原油タンカーが米封鎖を突破できていないため、買い手は９月下旬以降に納入される新たなイラン産原油を事実上入手できなくなる可能性がある」と記した。

item.title: Snoring, subways and stealth ads: how big pharma targets China's waistline
item.description: Weight-loss drugmakers, vying to tighten the belts of Chinese consumers, are promoting obesity awareness in metro stations, exercise studios and soccer stadiums as local restrictions prevent the direct advertising of prescription medicines in the world’s second-largest drug market.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Silver
item.content:encoded: Weight-loss drugmakers, vying to tighten the belts of Chinese consumers, are promoting obesity awareness in metro stations, exercise studios and soccer stadiums as local restrictions prevent the direct advertising of prescription medicines in the world’s second-largest drug market. China's rate of overweight or obese people could reach more than 65% by 2030, the country's National Health Commission [USN:L4N3LY0BH TEXT:"has said"]. Novo Nordisk (NOVOb.CO) , Eli Lilly (LLY.N) , Pfizer (PFE.N) and local firm Innovent Biologics (1801.HK) are competing for market share with their versions of once-weekly GLP-1 weight-loss injections in China. Lilly led the once-weekly GLP-1 sales on Alibaba's (9988.HK) Tmall e-commerce platform and JD.com (9618.HK) in the second quarter, according to Jefferies. China does not allow drug companies to advertise prescription medicines directly to consumers. They can provide information to the public about the risks of specific diseases and recommend that they engage with doctors. Campaigns cannot mention product names, but might indirectly encourage people to seek help. "Don't forget to pay attention to Dad's snoring and promptly visit a respiratory department or sleep center," a banner with a Lilly logo advised commuters recently at a metro station in Shanghai’s central Jingan district. Snoring is a common symptom of sleep apnea, which is [USN:L4N3YZ0BR TEXT:"strongly linked"] to being overweight. Lilly's GLP-1 drug Mounjaro has been shown in clinical trials to alleviate the condition. Ads from Innovent and e-commerce giant Meituan (3690.HK) displayed on a wall in the same station last month said "scientific weight management" can reverse fatty liver disease. Another ad at a soccer stadium in Suzhou during a July match said “Innovent Biologics weight loss amazing!” repeatedly, a stream on the Weibo social media platform showed. Gym chain Supermonkey touted via social media platform Xiaohongshu a partnership with Pfizer to launch a “healthy weight loss party” in June and July. A Pfizer employee told a crowd at one such party in Shanghai that the company hoped to help them build a lasting, healthy way of life. Afterward, a trainer led a weightlifting session for attendees, a post by the drugmaker on Xiaohongshu - which was later deleted - showed. The communication efforts of drugmakers go well beyond campaigns related to other medicines, said Jia Hepeng, a professor of science communication at Soochow University in Suzhou. “I rarely see pharmaceutical companies promoting prescription drugs for hypertension, tumors, and other diseases in public settings, or even through indirect advertising,” Jia said. Social media promotions, along with recommendations from friends and family, have led some patients to seek specific weight-loss medicines by name, employees at hospitals in Shanghai and Guangzhou told Reuters. At first, patients asked for Novo’s semaglutide, also known as Wegovy, but recently Lilly’s tirzepatide, also known as Mounjaro, and Innovent’s mazdutide, also known as Xinermei, have been requested more frequently, said Zhao Xiaolong, an endocrinologist at the Shanghai Public Health Clinical Center. MATCHING COMPETITORS Novo launched the first once-weekly GLP-1 for weight management in China in late 2024. Lilly and Innovent [USN:L6N3UH05G TEXT:"followed"] in January 2025 and July 2025, respectively, while the first prescriptions for Pfizer's [USN:L6N4150ND TEXT:"Xianweiying"] were issued in April. Sales of GLP-1 therapies for weight management could reach 30 billion yuan ($4 billion) in the next five to seven years, up from an estimated 3 billion to 4 billion yuan at present, said Yang Huang, J.P. Morgan's head of China healthcare research. Novo executive Cai Yan [USN:L6N3YV0I7 TEXT:"became"] the firm's Greater China president in March. She soon heard from doctors in China that the company's communications were weak compared with its competitors, Cai told Reuters. Some Novo rivals were more bold, talking about the benefits of a drug more directly in their messaging, she said. "I focus very much on what we should do and what is the right thing to do, what we can learn from competitors," she said. "If you feel a competitor is much better in communication, layman language to the public, then we have to transform the way, how we communicate, from (a) medical educational perspective." She said Novo is changing its approach to not only focus on doctors in hospitals, but to reach patients with information on obesity via different types of media. The drugmaker aims to make the language in its public communication more accessible. Last month, Novo and state broadcaster CCTV held a health exhibit on a street in Beijing with group dancing, Novo said on WeChat, a messaging app. Text displayed at the exhibit said some GLP-1 therapies have been validated in multiple, large-scale clinical studies, a separate post from one Xiaohongshu user showed. Some weight-management campaigns could also cross a line into drug advertising, medical and legal experts said. For example, Innovent and Meituan's subway billboards might lead consumers to associate them with a specific prescription weight-loss drug, said Chen Zhenggang, a partner at DeHeng Law Offices in Beijing. The billboards did not explicitly display the names of Innovent's product - Xinermei or mazdutide - but included what appeared to be a mascot with a similar-sounding name: "Madudu." “On one side, they're definitely trying to be compliant ... on the other side, you have drugs and you want to sell," said J.P. Morgan analyst Huang, referring to obesity awareness and educational programs in China. Earlier this year, Lilly [USN:L4N41E0RC TEXT:"paused"] its local obesity awareness campaign in India after the nation's drug regulator said the company's awareness campaign there had coincided with Mounjaro's India launch and could potentially promote the drug to consumers. In a statement, Lilly said its educational activities do not promote any specific medicines and it is "consistent" with China's health strategies. Pfizer, Innovent, Meituan and China's market regulator declined or did not respond to requests for comment.

item.title: ヘッジファンド､ドル安に備え-米財務省が利回り管理なら信認に打撃も
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ベッセント米財務長官は、米政府の借り入れコスト上昇に対応し、財政再建に一層重点を置く新たな取り組みを近く発表する。詳細の公表を控え、ヘッジファンドはドルの弱気ポジションに積み上げつつある。

米財務省が19日、長期国債の買い戻し上限額を2倍以上に増額すると発表したことを受け、ドル相場は1日としては過去約3週間で最大の下落率を記録。そうした圧力は21日も顕著に表れ、ドルは下げを拡大した。

バークレイズのG10外国為替トレーディング共同責任者トルステン・シェーンボルン氏は、複雑なデリバティブ（金融派生商品）ではなく、ストレートな為替取引の領域（リニア領域）に言及し、「特にヘッジファンドの顧客から顕著な反応が見られた。8月を通じてドルの供給が持続する中で、ドル売りが加速した」と分析した。ただ中長期的に安定的利益を目指す投資資金、リアルマネーにはそれほど方向感がなかったという。

米政府の借り入れコスト抑制を目指すベッセント財務長官の積極的アプローチに対し、一部投資家は、最終的にドルが代償を支払うことになり、米財務省が積極的な利回りの管理にかじを切れば、ドルの信認が弱まると考えている。

ドルを巡る悲観論は、オプション市場でもはっきりうかがえる。ブルームバーグの指標によると、今後1カ月のドル下落に備えるオプション価格（プレミアム）は、上昇リスクに備えるヘッジコストと比べ、今年2月以来で最も高くなった。

シティグループのアジア外為オプション取引責任者、アクシャイ・サクセナ氏（シンガポール在勤）は「米財務省による長期国債買い戻しの増額発表以降、外為オプション市場の至る所でドルの下落に備えるヘッジの需要がより広範に確認された」と指摘した。

サクセナ氏によれば、スイスフランのインプライド・ボラティリティー（IV）に最も急激な価格の再評価が反映された。IVは通貨の将来の変動率を予測する指標であり、オプションのプレミアムに直接影響を与える。
